issues.failure_explanation: The claim JP^{-1}D = P^{-1}JD requires P^{-1}D to commute with J. The matrix P^{-1}D involves the unitary matrices Q_j from Lemma 3 applied to the SVD of V_j. For these to commute with J_j (which has distinct scalar blocks in the semi-simple case), the SVD of V_j = diag(V_{j1}, V_{j4}) must be chosen to respect the block structure (block-diagonal U and V). diagnostic_evidence.quote: Denote by $Q_j=\m\boxed{diag}(Q_{j1},Q_{j2})$. Then, we have $$\tilde{S}_j:=D_{jj}^{-1}Q_j\begin{bmatrix} 0 & S_1\\ -\epsilon S_1^H & 0\\ \end{bmatrix}Q_j^HD_{jj}^{-1}

issues.failure_explanation: The normalization has multiple errors. (1) The congruence Q_j(…)Q_j^H is wrong; with SVD S_j = Q_{j1}D_j Q_{j2}^H, the correct congruence is Q_j^H(…)Q_j (giving Q_{j1}^H S_j Q_{j2} = D_j). Q_j(…)Q_j^H yields Q_{j1}^2 D_j (Q_{j2}^H)^2 ≠ D_j. (2) The formula uses S_1 instead of S_j (subscript error). (3) For the |λ_j|=1 case in the semi-simple setting, the full block Γ_j is 2n_j×2n_j but the proof normalizes only an n_j×n_j sub-block, ignoring the off-diagonal coupling S_{j2}. The normalization of the full Hermitian/skew-Hermitian block requires unitary diagonalization of the entire block.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the normalization using the correct congruence Q_j^H(…)Q_j and normalize the full 2n_j×2n_j block Γ_j (which is Hermitian or skew-Hermitian) via unitary diagonalization, rather than individual sub-blocks.
issues.overall_effect: The normalization of Γ in the H-palindromic semi-simple case is not correctly established. The claimed normal form of Γ is correct in principle but the proof's construction does not achieve it.
issues.title: H-palindromic semi-simple normalization uses wrong congruence and wrong matrix
issues.why_classification: The proof's normalization construction is wrong and needs to be redone with a different (though contained) approach — diagonalizing the full block — rather than a local formula fix. The conclusion remains correct and no claims are lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof applies Theorem 1's construction which requires [X̃; X̃Λ̃] to be nonsingular. The proof states this as a conditional ('if there exists') but then sets X̃_1 = X_1Φ without verifying nonsingularity. Nonsingularity can fail: when the new eigenvalues σ(Λ̃_1) overlap with the kept eigenvalues σ(Λ_2), the matrix [X_1Φ, X_2; X_1ΦΛ̃_1, X_2Λ_2] has linearly dependent block-columns (e.g., when Λ̃_1 = Λ_2 the two block-columns are identical). The standing assumptions σ(Λ_1)∩σ(Λ̃_1)=∅ and σ(Λ_1)∩σ(Λ_2^{-★})=∅ do not exclude this overlap.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either add the hypothesis σ(Λ̃_1)∩σ(Λ_2)=∅ (requiring new eigenvalues to be distinct from kept ones) and prove nonsingularity under it, or prove nonsingularity from the existing assumptions if possible. At minimum, the theorem's universal quantifier over Φ and Γ̃_1 must be restricted to cases where [X̃; X̃Λ̃] is nonsingular.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem's claim that the formulas give a solution of Problem 2 for 'any' Φ and Γ̃_1 is not established; the construction can produce an ill-defined or non-solution when the prescribed new eigenvalues coincide with kept eigenvalues.
issues.title: EEP theorem does not establish nonsingularity of updated Vandermonde-type matrix
issues.why_classification: A limited strengthening of hypotheses (adding eigenvalue non-overlap) preserves the method and comparable result. Alternatively, a contained argument for nonsingularity under existing hypotheses would suffice. Neither requires new proof architecture nor major loss of scope.
